contentChunks.htmlValue: Usage

Use progress indicators to show the status of ongoing processes, such as loading an app, submitting a form, or saving updates.

When multiple items are loading, use a single progress indicator to show progress for the group. Don’t add progress indicators to every activity.

contentChunks.footer: Indicate overall progress of a group of items
contentChunks.altText: One progress indicator showing the loading progress for a page of podcasts.

contentChunks.footer: Don’t show the progress of each activity in a group
contentChunks.altText: Two progress indicators showing the loading progress of two podcasts.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Choose a loading or progress indicator that corresponds to the expected wait time and kind of process. 

If the wait is very long, consider allowing people to navigate away from the page while the process finishes up.

Expected wait time
Recommendation
Instant (under 200ms)No indicator
Short (between 200ms and 5s)Loading indicator
Long (Over 5s)Progress indicator

contentChunks.footer: Instant (under 200ms): Display the content immediately
contentChunks.altText: Screen without latency without progress indicator.

contentChunks.footer: Short (between 200ms and 5s): Use a loading indicator
contentChunks.altText: Screen with slight lag with loading indicator.

contentChunks.footer: Long (over 5s): Use a progress indicator
contentChunks.altText: Screen with long lag and progress indicator.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
There are two variants of progress indicators:

  1. Linear

  2. Circular

Linear indicators are best when placed on the edge of a container.

Circular indicators are best when centered in an element.

A process should be represented by the same variant of progress indicator throughout the product. For example, if refreshing uses a circular indicator in one place, it should use circular indicators everywhere.

contentChunks.footer:
1. Linear indicator  
  2. Circular indicator
contentChunks.altText: 1. A primary colored horizontal line fills a contrasting track from left to right. 2. A circle appears from 0 to 360 degrees.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Progress indicators behave differently based on the time of progress being tracked:

  • Determinate: Known progress and wait time
  • Indeterminate: Unknown progress and wait time

When using a determinate indicator, the indicator must accurately represent the progress of what it's measuring. 

Use indeterminate indicators to show that a process is happening, but the wait time is unknown.

contentChunks.footer:
1. Determinate progress indicators fill from 0% to 100%
  2. Indeterminate progress indicators move along a fixed track, growing and shrinking in size
contentChunks.altText: Linear and circular progress indicators show both determinate and indeterminate progress.

contentChunks.htmlValue: As more information about a process becomes available, a progress indicator should change from indeterminate to determinate.

contentChunks.footer: A linear progress indicator changes from indeterminate to determinate while loading a screen
contentChunks.altText: On a track, a contrasting primary-colored horizontal line grows and shrinks, then fills it from left to right as app loads.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Anatomy

contentChunks.footer:
1. Active indicator
  2. Track
  3. Stop indicator
contentChunks.altText: 1. The track is a horizontal line. 2. A primary colored line over the contrasting colored track is the progress indicator.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Active indicator

The active indicator shows the progress that has been made so far. 

In indeterminate processes, it grows and shrinks along the track repeatedly.

contentChunks.footer: Linear indicators animate from the leading to the trailing edge along the track. Circular indicators animate from the top of the track, clockwise by default.
contentChunks.altText: A primary colored horizontal line fills a contrasting line from left to right.

contentChunks.htmlValue: The active indicator appears as soon as progress begins. At low percentages where space is limited, this should appear as a dot to help people understand that there’s progress underway.

contentChunks.footer: When progress first begins, the active indicator appears as a dot
contentChunks.altText: A linear and circular progress indicator at 1% progress, where the active indicator has only just appeared.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
The active indicator has two shape options: flat and wavy. Use the shape that best fits the product’s tone.

The wavy shape can make longer processes feel less static and is best used when a more expressive style is appropriate.

When using the wavy shape, the overall height of the component changes. At very small sizes, the wavy shape may not be as visible.

contentChunks.footer: Wavy linear indicators increase the height of the overall container
contentChunks.altText: Examples of flat and wavy active indicator.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Stop indicator

The stop indicator is a 4dp circle that marks the end of a linear determinate progress indicator to meet Material's accessibility standards.

It's not used for indeterminate or circular progress indicators.

The stop indicator is required if the track has a contrast below 3:1 with its container or the surface behind the container.

contentChunks.footer: Use a stop indicator when placing the progress indicator inside a container with low contrast
contentChunks.altText: A primary colored horizontal  line fills a contrasting line from left to right.

contentChunks.footer: Only remove the end stop indicator if there's a visual contrast of at least 3:1 with surrounding surfaces
contentChunks.altText: An invisible circular track fills with color from 0 to 360 degrees.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Placement

Place a linear progress indicator along the edge of a container that’s loading. If the container changes shape, place it on the edge that animates. It can also be placed in the middle of a container.

Use a single progress indicator at the top of a page to show progress of the whole group. Don’t add one for every element unless they’re activated independently.

contentChunks.footer: When at the top of a screen, a progress indicator shows that all of the page content is loading
contentChunks.altText: Progress indicator at top of screen, indicating page content is loading.

contentChunks.footer: When attached to a card, a progress indicator shows that just the card content is loading
contentChunks.altText: Progress indicator on a card, indicating that the card's content is loading.

contentChunks.footer: A progress indicator on the expanding edge of a card shows that the edge may expand to show the loaded content
contentChunks.altText: Linear indicator shows the loading progress of a selected news article in a list.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Circular progress indicators should be centered directly on the container or page that's loading, such as a button or card.

When loading more items on a page, place the circular progress indicator in the empty space where the new content will appear, not overlapping existing content.

However, if the content does not take long to load, consider using a loading indicator instead.

contentChunks.footer: A circular progress indicator can show that the page is loading
contentChunks.altText: As content loads, the screen is blank except for a circular progress indicator.

contentChunks.footer: A circular progress indicator can show where new items will appear on a page. A loading indicator also works well in this space.
contentChunks.altText: As container content loads, the container is blank except for a circular progress indicator.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Progress indicators in buttons

A circular indicator can be placed in a button to show that the button’s action is currently in progress.

In very small buttons, use the flat shape since the wavy shape is not as visible at that size.

To ensure a minimum 3:1 contrast ratio, change the active indicator color to be the same color as the button’s icon or label text, and remove the track.

contentChunks.footer: Use circular indicators for short, indeterminate activities under 5 seconds
contentChunks.altText: Determinate circular indicator active for 2 seconds after download button is selected, reflecting download progress.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid applying progress indicators to every button in a list
contentChunks.altText: Shows idea of indeterminate circular indicators active on multiple buttons as  cluttered and confusing.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Responsive layout

Right-to-left languages

Linear progress indicators should be mirrored horizontally for products using right-to-left (RTL) languages. 

Circular progress indicators don’t need to be mirrored.

contentChunks.footer: Linear progress indicators can flow from right to left in right-to-left (RTL) languages
contentChunks.altText: Mirrored right-to-left progress indicator.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Large screens

Circular progress indicators have flexible sizes. They can range from 24dp to 240dp, depending on the placement and the breakpoint. Avoid exceeding the minimum and maximum sizes.

Reserve very large progress indicators for large and extra-large windows, such as desktop.

contentChunks.footer: The waveform should scale with the size so the proportions look the same across sizes
contentChunks.altText: Circular progress indicators can range in size from 24dps to 240dps.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
Linear progress indicators dynamically adjust to fit the width of the window or element they’re placed within, such as a card. They shouldn’t be used in any elements smaller than 40dp.

The padding on each end should be 4dp minimum, but can be modified.

contentChunks.footer: The linear progress indicator should always span the width of the UI element it’s placed within
contentChunks.altText: Linear progress indicators can dynamically adjust to any width.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Use cases

People should be able to do the following using the assistive technology:

  • Navigate to the progress indicator
  • Understand what progress the indicator is communicating
Interaction & style
The active indicator, which displays progress, provides visual contrast of at least 3:1 against most background colors.

contentChunks.footer: The progress indicator and stop indicator provide visual contrast of at least 3:1 against most background colors
contentChunks.altText: Dark line of progress indicator stands out against the lighter colored track.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
When integrated into another component, such as a button, make sure that the active indicator provides visual contrast of at least 3:1 against the other component. 

For the active indicator, use the same color as the label text or icon. The track should be removed.

contentChunks.footer: Ensure the indicator’s color provides at least 3:1 contrast against the surface it's on
contentChunks.altText: Circular indicator on button passes 3 to 1 contrast test.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid using a color below 3:1 contrast
contentChunks.altText: Circular indicator on button fails 3 to 1 contrast test.

contentChunks.htmlValue:
For linear progress indicators, the stop indicator is required if the track has a contrast below 3:1 with its container or the surface behind the container.

Essentially, the end of the track must be easy to identify.

contentChunks.footer: Only remove the stop indicator when the linear progress indicator has at least a 3:1 color contrast with surrounding containers and surfaces
contentChunks.altText: Bright container holding the progress bar is on a dark surface, passing the 3:1 color contrast.

contentChunks.footer: Avoid removing the stop indicator if any adjacent containers or surfaces are below the 3:1 color contrast
contentChunks.altText: Bright container holding progress indicator is on a bright surface, failing the 3:1 color contrast.

contentChunks.htmlValue: Labeling elements

Since the progress indicator is a visual cue, it needs an accessibility label to describe the kind and amount of progress made.

Use the progress bar accessibility role, and write an accessibility label that describes the purpose of the progress indicator. The label should include the process, such as "loading,” and the affected content, such as a page, article, or episode. For example: "Loading news article" or "Refreshing page."

contentChunks.footer: Progress indicator labels should explain which items are loading
contentChunks.altText: Determinate linear progress indicator has an accessibility label of “loading news article” and role of “progressbar”.

contentChunks.footer: A label on an intedeterminate progress indicator on a screen which is loading a set of podcast episodes
contentChunks.altText: Indeterminate linear progress indicator has an accessibility label of “loading my episodes” and role of “progressbar.”
